extracted.intended_audience: WAN-IFRA members, senior media executives, newsroom leaders, publishers, and researchers interested in global newspaper industry trends
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate the annual World Press Trends industry report describing the current and future state of the global newspaper/news media industry, based on a global executive survey and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-Term business prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of mid-term business prospects for publishers (included as a chapter item under Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Chapter 1: Business Outlook. Intended to capture publishers' view of medium-term viability and strategic direction; based on survey responses from senior media executives and newsroom leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenues in the next 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecasts and expectations for revenues over the coming 12 months (listed under Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate short-term financial outlook; informed by survey data across 66 countries and contrasted with historical trends in the annual study.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of play: The role of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of how AI is affecting publishers and the news media industry (a 'state of play' subtopic in Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers adoption, impact, and publisher sentiment toward AI as reported by senior executives; useful for assessing technology-driven strategic risks and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of play: Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of the role and impact of search (platforms/algorithms) on the news media business (a 'state of play' subtopic in Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses search-driven distribution, traffic, and revenue implications; draws on executives' perspectives and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of play: Creators and the creator economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration of the creator economy and its relationship with publishers (a 'state of play' subtopic in Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines trends around creators, new revenue/partnership models, and how publishers position themselves relative to creator-led content ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of play: Relationships with tech platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of publishers' relationships with technology platforms and their effects on the industry (a 'state of play' subtopic in Business Outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers collaboration, competition, policy and commercial arrangements between publishers and major tech platforms as reported by survey participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: The big picture (Revenue Trends)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level overview of revenue trends across the newspaper industry (listed as first item under Chapter 2: Revenue Trends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets context for more specific revenue topics; aggregates survey findings and trend analysis to show overall direction of publisher revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for the post-print era
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies and planning for an industry transition away from print (a Revenue Trends subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on how publishers are adapting business models, operations and revenue strategies in anticipation of reduced print volumes and circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital reader revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of revenues generated from digital readers (subscriptions, memberships, micropayments) (a Revenue Trends subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines effectiveness of digital reader monetization strategies and trends reported by publishers in the survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Trends and performance of digital advertising as a revenue stream (a Revenue Trends subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers programmatic, direct-sold, platform-dependent advertising and how digital ad revenues are evolving for publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of alternative or non-core revenue streams beyond reader revenue and digital advertising (a Revenue Trends subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include events, commercial services, licensing, e-commerce, and other diversification strategies noted in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and outgoings
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of publisher costs and outgoings that impact competitiveness and profitability (Chapter 3: The Cost of Staying Competitive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates expense structures, key cost drivers, and how costs influence strategic choices; informed by survey responses and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of publishers' investment priorities (Chapter 3 subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights areas where publishers are allocating capital and resources (e.g., technology, journalism, product development) to stay competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Freedom — Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: A general overview of the state of media freedom globally (Chapter 4: Media Freedom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the chapter's findings and situates media freedom as a key industry concern assessed via survey data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Freedom — What our data shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of empirical findings from the study about media freedom (Chapter 4 subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes survey evidence and patterns revealing the current condition of press freedom across jurisdictions covered by the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Freedom — How media freedom is being threatened
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and analysis of threats to media freedom (Chapter 4 subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses specific pressures (political, legal, economic, technological) reported by respondents that undermine press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Freedom — Unpacking the causes and moving forward
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of root causes behind media freedom challenges and suggested ways forward (Chapter 4 subtopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores drivers of media freedom decline and proposes approaches, informed by data and case study insights, for mitigation and policy responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: comprehensive executive survey
rubrics_metrics.description: The study is grounded in a comprehensive survey of senior media executives and newsroom leaders — more than 170 participants across 66 countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological note signals the report's empirical basis and geographic breadth; useful as a criterion for evaluating the report's representativeness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case studies from around the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of case studies that provide practical examples and context for the report's findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case studies are used alongside survey insights to offer a fresh perspective on the health of the news industry and illustrate how trends play out in different markets.
